summary.text:
Let me analyze the requirements.

State: LeadA (retained), previous_demand, episode_served.

At scan:
- Sample inputs.
- Determine outputs based on Demand, FaultA, FaultB, current LeadA (qLeadA pre-scan).
- computed: if Demand:
  - if LeadA: if !FaultA -> PumpA, elif !FaultB -> PumpB (fallback). Wait LeadA is preference for A. If LeadA true, prefer A. If A faulted, fallback B if healthy.
  - if !LeadA: prefer B, if faulted fallback A.
  - PumpA = Demand & ((LeadA & !FaultA) | (!LeadA & FaultB & !FaultA))
  - Actually: PumpA = Demand & !FaultA & (LeadA | FaultB)
  - PumpB = Demand & !FaultB & (!LeadA | FaultA)
  - Check never both: if LeadA true, PumpA requires !FaultA; PumpB requires FaultA (and !LeadA) -> can't both. Good.
- episode_served: track if any pump ran during current continuous demand episode. Set when Demand & (PumpA|PumpB) at any scan.
- On falling edge of Demand (previous_demand true, current Demand false): completedServed = episode_served (from the episode). If completedServed, toggle LeadA. Reset episode_served.
- P7: !completedServed -> LeadA <-> qLeadA. So when not completedServed, LeadA stays.

Note ordering: completedServed uses episode_served state. At falling edge, episode_served should include scans up through last demand scan.

Implementation:

VAR
  LeadA : BOOL := TRUE;
  prevDemand : BOOL := FALSE;
  episodeServed : BOOL := FALSE;
END_VAR

Body:
```
VAR
  runA, runB : BOOL;
  completedServed : BOOL;
END_VAR

// determine which pumps run
runA := Demand AND NOT FaultA AND (LeadA OR FaultB);
runB := Demand AND NOT FaultB AND ((NOT LeadA) OR FaultA);

PumpA := runA;
PumpB := runB;

completedServed := prevDemand AND NOT Demand AND episodeServed;

IF completedServed THEN
    LeadA := NOT LeadA;
END_IF

IF Demand THEN
    IF runA OR runB THEN
        episodeServed := TRUE;
    END_IF
ELSE
    episodeServed := FALSE;
END_IF

prevDemand := Demand;
```

Wait check falling edge: completedServed computed from prevDemand (pre-scan previous demand) and episodeServed pre-scan. Since episodeServed at pre-scan includes the last demand scan. Good.

But careful: when completedServed, we toggle LeadA, then Demand false so episodeServed reset to false. Fine.

Test order matters: episodeServed computation after LeadA toggle doesn't affect output this scan since Pump outputs already assigned. LeadA output is toggled same scan - correct per P6.

Let me check test alternate:
Step0: Demand F -> runA F, runB F. lead true. episodeServed false. prevDemand false. Outputs correct.
Step1: Demand T, faults F. runA = T & T & (T or F)=T. runB = T&T&(!T or F)= F. Outputs PumpA T, LeadA T. episodeServed=T. prevDemand=T.
Step2: same, T. episodeServed stays T.
Step3: Demand F. completedServed = prevDemand(T) & !Demand & episodeServed(T) = T. LeadA toggle -> F. episodeServed=false. prevDemand=F. Outputs: runA = F. PumpA F, PumpB F, LeadA F. Correct.
Step4: Demand F. completedServed false. LeadA stays F. Correct (only LeadA expected).
Step5: Demand T. runA = T&!(F)&(LeadA(F) or FaultB(F)) = F. runB = T&!F&(!LeadA(T) or F)=T. PumpB T, LeadA F. Correct.
Step6: Demand F. completedServed = T & T & episodeServed(T)=T -> toggle LeadA->T. Correct.

Fallback test:
Step0: Demand T both faulted. runA = T & !FaultA(F) ... = F. runB = T & !FaultB(F)... = F. Both off, LeadA true. episodeServed false (no run). prevDemand T.
Step1: Demand F, both faulted. completedServed = prevDemand(T)&!Demand&T & episodeServed(F)=F. LeadA stays true. Correct.
Step2: Demand T, FaultA T, FaultB F. runA = T & !FaultA(F) = F. runB = T & !FaultB(T) & (!LeadA(F) or FaultA(T)) = T. PumpB T, LeadA true. episodeServed=T. prevDemand=T.
Step3: Demand T, faults F. runA = T&T&(LeadA(T) or FaultB(F))=T. runB = T & !F(F)=T & (!LeadA(F) or FaultA(F))=F. PumpA T, LeadA T. episodeServed T.
Step4: Demand F, both faulted. completedServed = T&T&episodeServed(T)=T -> toggle LeadA->F. Correct.

All good.

END_VAR
VAR

    runB : BOOL;

END_VAR
```
